parts.note: a famous golf club at St Andrews, whose name read literally describes a king who is both regal and very old

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which golf club would best fit an aged king.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal and Ancient at St Andrews in Scotland is the historic governing golf club; 'Club' looks like a stick to swing but is the society.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the St Andrews golf club literally pairs kingly with old, matching an elderly monarch.

definitions.meaning: forward or amorous approaches made to someone
sums a publisher pays an author before a book earns royalties

explanation.surface: An author complains of brazen conduct from the firm that publishes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: forward approaches, and money paid ahead of royalties.

definitions.meaning: a great number, as in a multitude

explanation.surface: A man who throws plenty of parties.
explanation.definitionFit: One who receives guests, and also a word for a large crowd or great number.

indicators.note: uncovering suggests the letters of the following words are opened up and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps called Ray, digs up an unusual discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name but is a beam of radiation; 'uncovering' rearranges RAREFIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared describes a kind of radiation, so an infrared beam is an example of a ray.

parts.note: to arm is to equip for defence, so protect
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is shielded from the ships of a navy.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one of 1588.

indicators.note: about means the song's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a carol is a song, especially a Christmas one
USA stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A gathering sings a tune about the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a noisy drinking party, a synonym for a revel.

indicators.note: in says the Irish name sits inside the doctor's letters

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A vet tends sheep somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The merino is a breed of sheep prized for its fine wool.

clue.text: Point to orders actor should obey

definitions.text: Point to orders actor should obey

parts.words: Point to orders actor should obey
parts.note: the instructions in a play's script telling performers where to move, read as pointing out their orders

explanation.surface: A director indicates the commands a performer must follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes in a script tell performers how and where to move, so they are orders actors obey.

parts.note: odd means unusual
to corner a market is to hold a monopoly of it

explanation.surface: A remote spot is chosen for a strange business monopoly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monopoly' may suggest the board game, but it means control of a market, a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd corner is an idiom for a remote or out-of-the-way spot.

parts.note: ale is a drink, a beer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a quick drink is in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means quick-witted and on the ball, a synonym of quick.

clue.text: He makes adjustments more suitable to modern times

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the era running to modern times
apter is the comparative of apt, more suitable

explanation.surface: A reformer brings things up to date to suit the present age.
explanation.walkthrough: AD is Anno Domini, the dating label for the present era.
explanation.definitionFit: One who adapts things makes adjustments, so the noun fits a person who modifies.

clue.text: Paying high regard to a party combination

parts.note: a do is a party
a ring is a combination, a group working together

explanation.surface: Someone admires a coalition of political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests politics but is a do, a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring someone means worshipping or esteeming them greatly.

indicators.note: returning means the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A painter returns to his companion to take a bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns RA into AR; CH is the British honour Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved shape, the same as a bow.

parts.note: broads is American slang for women
one's word is one's honour, as in word of honour

explanation.surface: Women in the States honour an ancient arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a wide-bladed sword, a weapon of earlier times.

indicators.note: in this across clue, to support means coming after the other piece
show here is read as putting on a display of the letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, the first part of sideshow
a red is a revolutionary, a communist

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is sought to back a fairground attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits the single word 'sideshow' into its two halves: 'show' is the anagram signal working on the first half. A fairground picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired and wanted are synonyms, both meaning longed for.

parts.note: the roof is the ceiling of a building
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A support beam stands in for the top of an actor's set.
explanation.walkthrough: Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated English actor-manager of the 1890s.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftree is the ridge beam of a roof, the same as a ridgepole.

parts.note: de is French for of
liver is offal eaten as meat

explanation.surface: A French butcher hands over some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as the verb hand over, run together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver something is to hand it over to someone.

indicators.note: the In at the start of Indeed says the pipe goes inside what follows

parts.note: taken as written, the rest of Indeed
a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the pipe was removed and gets a firm yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to split the exclamation 'Indeed!' into 'In' and 'deed', so the word that seems to be an assent supplies both container and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deducted means subtracted, which is to say taken away.

clue.text: Farewell to Inca characters from Spanish city

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: characters suggests the letters of Inca are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller bids goodbye to the Incas and leaves a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a major city on Spain's eastern coast.

clue.text: Sailor having to go round with singer

parts.note: Horatio Nelson was Britain's most famous sailor
to eddy is to swirl round

explanation.surface: A seaman must go round with a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson Eddy was an American baritone of 1930s film musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Eddy was a famous American singer and film star.

clue.text: Hang about to see strange rite

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of rite are turned into an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone lingers to watch an odd ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, to hang about.

definitions.meaning: to get away from or avoid
a leak or outflow, as of gas

explanation.surface: Dodging the question.
explanation.definitionFit: To get free is to evade; a leak of gas is an issue of it.

clue.text: Pass back to leading brain in power group

indicators.note: to means the turned pass is added on after the leading letter
leading means take the first letter of brain
back means the word for a pass is read in reverse

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A footballer passes back to the team's leading thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like football but is COL, a mountain pass; 'back' gives LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties united to wield power.

clue.text: To have a nincompoop in charge is unwise

parts.note: an idiot is a nincompoop

explanation.surface: Putting a fool in command is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means foolish, so it is a synonym for unwise.

clue.text: Wine Scotsman has terrible itch to swallow

indicators.note: to swallow means the jumbled letters take the name inside them
terrible says the letters of itch are badly jumbled

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot with an awful itch gulps down some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges ITCH to CHTI, which takes in IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

indicators.note: the 's reads as has, saying the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A bloom grows on a Shetland island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a Shetland island famous for knitwear; the answer sits across its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a flowering plant with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: She brings back some piece intact

indicators.note: brings back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman returns a fragment unbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ECEIN from 'piece intact'; 'brings back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, so she stands for the word.

parts.note: p, piano, means quiet in music
revision is study done for exams, homework

explanation.surface: A pupil shows foresight by studying quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage revision means studying for exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevision is seeing ahead, the same as foresight.
